tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the woman say she will do?

options.A: Reply to the man’s last proposal within a short time.
options.B: Sign the agreement if one small change is made to it.
options.C: Make a sponsorship deal for her client at the meeting.
options.D: Give the man some good news regarding the contract.

questions.cn: 女士说她将做什么？

optionsCn.A: 在短时间内回复男士上次的提案。
optionsCn.B: 只要做一处小改动就签这份协议。
optionsCn.C: 在会上为她的客户达成赞助协议。
optionsCn.D: 就合同给男士一些好消息。

questions.stem: What does the man say about some people he represents?

options.A: They are becoming impatient.
options.B: They are afraid time is running out.
options.C: They are used to making alterations.
options.D: They are concerned about the details.

questions.cn: 男士说他代表的某些人怎么样？

optionsCn.A: 他们正变得不耐烦。
optionsCn.B: 他们担心时间不多了。
optionsCn.C: 他们习惯于做修改。
optionsCn.D: 他们关心细节。

questions.stem: What reason does the woman give for the new deal to exclude the Middle East?

options.A: To prevent geographical discrimination.
options.B: To tap the food and beverage market.
options.C: To avoid any conflict of interest.
options.D: To reduce unfair competition.

questions.cn: 女士给出了什么理由，要求新协议把中东排除在外？

optionsCn.A: 为了防止地域歧视。
optionsCn.B: 为了开拓食品饮料市场。
optionsCn.C: 为了避免任何利益冲突。
optionsCn.D: 为了减少不公平竞争。

questions.stem: What does the man say about the Middle East?

options.A: It is a potential market for food and beverage.
options.B: It is very attractive for real estate developers.
options.C: It is a negligible market for his company.
options.D: It is very different from other markets.

questions.cn: 关于中东，男士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它是食品饮料的潜在市场。
optionsCn.B: 它对房地产开发商很有吸引力。
optionsCn.C: 对他的公司来说是微不足道的市场。
optionsCn.D: 它与其他市场非常不同。

lines.t: Thank you for meeting with me, Stephen, at such short notice.
lines.cn: 斯蒂芬，谢谢你这么临时还抽空见我。

lines.t: Not a problem.
lines.cn: 没问题。

lines.t: Margaret.
lines.cn: 玛格丽特。

lines.t: Now, please give me some good news.
lines.cn: 那么，请给我点好消息吧。

lines.t: Have you agreed to my last proposal?
lines.cn: 你同意我上次的提案了吗？

lines.t: I have, indeed.
lines.cn: 是的，我同意了。

lines.t: And I wish to sign the agreement pending one small change to be made to the contract.
lines.cn: 而且我希望能签这份协议，只要对合同做一处小改动。

lines.t: Margaret, we’ve been through this for almost a year now, back and forth, making alterations.
lines.cn: 玛格丽特，这件事我们已经来来回回谈了快一年，改了一遍又一遍。

lines.t: Are you sure you want to make a sponsorship deal for your clients, or not?
lines.cn: 你到底要不要为你的客户做这份赞助协议？

lines.t: I ask this, because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience.
lines.cn: 我这么问，是因为坦白说，我这边有些人已经快没耐心了。

lines.t: I understand your concerns.
lines.cn: 我理解你的顾虑。

lines.t: But as I’m sure you understand, we hold our clients’ best interests to be of the utmost concern.
lines.cn: 但想必你也明白，我们把客户的最大利益看得极为重要。

lines.t: We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts, rest assured, we all appreciate your firm’s patience.
lines.cn: 因此我们会把所有合同的细节都过一遍，请放心，我们都很感激贵公司的耐心。

lines.t: OK, fine.
lines.cn: 好，行。

lines.t: So what changes do you wish to make?
lines.cn: 那你想做什么改动？

lines.t: Essentially, we would like the new deal to exclude the Middle East.
lines.cn: 基本上，我们希望新协议把中东排除在外。

lines.t: That’s all.
lines.cn: 就这一处。

lines.t: The Middle East?
lines.cn: 中东？

lines.t: Why?
lines.cn: 为什么？

lines.t: My client has a couple of other prospective marketing deals from companies in the Middle East.
lines.cn: 我的客户还有几份来自中东公司的潜在营销合作。

lines.t: Those offers, should they materialize, would exclusively employ my client’s image in the Middle East only.
lines.cn: 那些合作如果谈成，将只在中东地区独家使用我客户的形象。

lines.t: Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically.
lines.cn: 因此，为避免任何冲突，我们需要确保两个营销活动在地域上不重叠。

lines.t: What business sector in the Middle East are we talking about here?
lines.cn: 这里说的是中东的哪个行业？

lines.t: Real estate.
lines.cn: 房地产。

lines.t: Well, that should be okay then.
lines.cn: 嗯，那应该没问题。

lines.t: So long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market, there should be no conflict of interest.
lines.cn: 只要产品与我们的食品饮料市场差别很大，就不会有利益冲突。

lines.t: Nevertheless, I will have to run this through my people.
lines.cn: 不过，我还得把这事交给我的人过一遍。

lines.t: I don’t foresee any problem, though.
lines.cn: 不过我看不出会有什么问题。

lines.t: The Middle East is a negligible market for us, but I still need to check this with a couple of departments.
lines.cn: 中东对我们来说是微不足道的市场，但我仍然需要和几个部门核实一下。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the woman say about all the astronomers at the Denver Observatory?

options.A: They are thrilled by a rare astronomic phenomenon.
options.B: They are celebrating a big event on mountain tops.
options.C: They are enthusiastic about big science-related stories.
options.D: They are joined by astronomers all across North America.

questions.cn: 关于丹佛天文台的所有天文学家，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们为一个罕见的天文现象而激动不已。
optionsCn.B: 他们正在山顶庆祝一件大事。
optionsCn.C: 他们对重大科学新闻充满热情。
optionsCn.D: 北美各地的天文学家都来和他们会合。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the conversation about the Oppenheimer comet?

options.A: It will be the most formidable of its kind in over a century.
options.B: It will come closest to Earth in more than one hundred years.
options.C: It will eclipse many other such events in human history.
options.D: It will be seen most clearly from Denver’s mountain tops.

questions.cn: 从对话中关于奥本海默彗星我们能了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它将是 100 多年来同类中最令人敬畏的一颗。
optionsCn.B: 它将在 100 多年里最接近地球。
optionsCn.C: 它将在人类历史上使许多同类事件相形见绌。
optionsCn.D: 从丹佛的山顶看它会最清楚。

questions.stem: What does the woman say people will only see in the sky without a telescope?

options.A: A blur.
options.B: Stars.
options.C: The edge of our galaxy.
options.D: An ordinary flying object.

questions.cn: 女士说没有望远镜的话，人们在天空中只能看到什么？

optionsCn.A: 一个模糊的光斑。
optionsCn.B: 星星。
optionsCn.C: 我们星系的边缘。
optionsCn.D: 一个普通的飞行物体。

questions.stem: What do scientists at the Denver Observatory advise amateurs do to facilitate their observation?

options.A: Use professional equipment.
options.B: Climb to the nearby heights.
options.C: Fix their eyes due north.
options.D: Make use of phone apps.

questions.cn: 丹佛天文台的科学家建议业余爱好者怎么做以便于观测？

optionsCn.A: 使用专业设备。
optionsCn.B: 爬到附近的高处。
optionsCn.C: 把目光固定在正北方向。
optionsCn.D: 利用手机应用。

lines.t: Next, we have a special science-related news story.
lines.cn: 接下来是一条特别的科学新闻。

lines.t: Paula Hancocks at the Denver Observatory.
lines.cn: 我们在丹佛天文台的葆拉·汉考克斯。

lines.t: Paula, what is the big story over there?
lines.cn: 葆拉，那边有什么大新闻？

lines.t: Hi, John.
lines.cn: 你好，约翰。

lines.t: Yes, all the astronomers on site here are very excited.
lines.cn: 是的，这里所有天文学家都非常兴奋。

lines.t: In fact, space enthusiasts all across North America and the rest of the Northern Hemisphere will be congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night’s sky.
lines.cn: 事实上，北美乃至整个北半球的天文爱好者今晚都会聚集在山顶上观星。

lines.t: Why?
lines.cn: 为什么？

lines.t: What’s the big event?
lines.cn: 有什么大事？

lines.t: Is there an eclipse happening soon?
lines.cn: 是快要有日食月食了吗？

lines.t: Tonight, the Earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet.
lines.cn: 今晚，地球将与奥本海默彗星近距离相会。

lines.t: It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years.
lines.cn: 这是我们这颗行星 100 多年来距离此类天象最近的一次。

lines.t: For this reason, it is expected that thousands of people will gaze up at the sky tonight in order to see this formidable object.
lines.cn: 正因如此，预计今晚会有成千上万人仰望夜空，观看这个令人敬畏的天体。

lines.t: How far away is this comet?
lines.cn: 这颗彗星有多远？

lines.t: Will people be able to see it with the naked eye?
lines.cn: 人们用肉眼能看到吗？

lines.t: The Oppenheimer comet will still be millions of miles away, on the edge of our galaxy.
lines.cn: 奥本海默彗星仍将在数百万英里之外，位于我们星系的边缘。

lines.t: But nevertheless, this is a relatively close distance, close enough for people to observe in good detail through a telescope.
lines.cn: 但尽管如此，这已是相对近的距离，近到人们可以用望远镜较清楚地观察。

lines.t: People will only see a blur without one.
lines.cn: 没有望远镜，人们只会看到一个模糊的光斑。

lines.t: However, that does not mean one needs professional equipment.
lines.cn: 不过，这并不意味着需要专业设备。

lines.t: Even the most ordinary of telescopes should be conducive for people to observe and wonder at this flying object.
lines.cn: 哪怕是最普通的望远镜，也应该足以让人观察并惊叹于这个飞行天体。

lines.t: Many of our viewers will be wondering how they too can take part in this once-in-a-lifetime event.
lines.cn: 我们许多观众都会想知道，他们怎样才能参与这场一生一次的活动。

lines.t: Where will this comet be in the sky?
lines.cn: 这颗彗星会在天空的什么位置？

lines.t: How can people find it?
lines.cn: 人们怎么找到它？

lines.t: The comet will be almost exactly due north, at 60 degrees above the equator.
lines.cn: 彗星将几乎正对正北方向，在赤道上方 60 度处。

lines.t: However, finding the comet is indeed very tricky.
lines.cn: 不过，要找到这颗彗星确实很不容易。

lines.t: And scientists here have told me there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this.
lines.cn: 这里的天文学家告诉我，有很多手机应用可以帮助做到这一点。

lines.t: How fantastic!
lines.cn: 太棒了！

lines.t: Thank you, Paula, for the information.
lines.cn: 谢谢你，葆拉，提供这些信息。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What question is said to have recently stirred debate?

options.A: Whether consumers should be warned against ultra-processed foods.
options.B: Whether there is sufficient scientific consensus on dietary guidelines.
options.C: Whether guidelines can form the basis for nutrition advice to consumers.
options.D: Whether food scientists will agree on the concept of ultra-processed foods.

questions.cn: 据说最近引发争论的是什么问题？

optionsCn.A: 是否应当警告消费者避免超加工食品。
optionsCn.B: 膳食指南是否存在充分的科学共识。
optionsCn.C: 指南能否成为向消费者提供营养建议的基础。
optionsCn.D: 食品科学家是否会对超加工食品的概念达成一致。

questions.stem: How does the system developed by Monteiro and colleagues classify foods?

options.A: By the labor cost for the final products.
options.B: By the degree of industrial processing.
options.C: By the extent of chemical alteration.
options.D: By the convention of classification.

questions.cn: 蒙泰罗及其同事开发的体系如何对食物分类？

optionsCn.A: 按最终产品的劳动力成本。
optionsCn.B: 按工业加工的程度。
optionsCn.C: 按化学改造的幅度。
optionsCn.D: 按分类的惯例。

questions.stem: What is consumption of ultra-processed foods linked with, according to studies?

options.A: Increased consumers’ expenses.
options.B: Greater risk of chronic diseases.
options.C: People’s misunderstanding of nutrition.
options.D: Children’s dislike for unprocessed foods.

questions.cn: 根据研究，超加工食品的摄入与什么有关？

optionsCn.A: 消费者开支增加。
optionsCn.B: 慢性病风险加大。
optionsCn.C: 人们对营养的误解。
optionsCn.D: 孩子对未加工食品的厌恶。

lines.t: Dietary guidelines form the basis for nutrition advice and regulations around the world.
lines.cn: 膳食指南是世界各地营养建议和法规的基础。

lines.t: While there is strong scientific consensus around most existing guidelines, one question has recently stirred debate: should consumers be warned to avoid ultra-processed foods?
lines.cn: 尽管对大多数现有指南存在很强的科学共识，但有一个问题最近引发了争论：是否应当警告消费者避免食用超加工食品？

lines.t: Two papers published today in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition outline the case for and against using the concept of ultra-processed foods to help inform dietary guidelines beyond conventional food classification systems.
lines.cn: 今天发表在《美国临床营养学杂志》上的两篇论文，分别陈述了支持和反对“在传统食物分类体系之外，用超加工食品这一概念来辅助制定膳食指南”的理由。

lines.t: The authors, Carlos Monteiro of the University of Sao Paulo and Arne Astrup of Novo Nordisk Foundation, will discuss the issue in a live virtual debate August 14th during NUTRITION 2024 LIVE ONLINE.
lines.cn: 两篇论文的作者——圣保罗大学的卡洛斯·蒙泰罗和新诺和诺德基金会的阿恩·阿斯特鲁普——将在 8 月 14 日“2024 营养学在线直播”的线上辩论中讨论这一问题。

lines.t: The debate centers around a system developed by Monteiro and colleagues that classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing, ranging from unprocessed to ultra-processed.
lines.cn: 争论的核心是蒙泰罗及其同事开发的一套体系，它按工业加工程度对食物分类，从未加工到超加工。

lines.t: The system defines ultra-processed foods as those made using sequences of processes that extract substances from foods and alter them with chemicals in order to formulate the final product.
lines.cn: 该体系把超加工食品定义为：通过一系列工艺从食物中提取物质、并用化学物质加以改造，从而配制成最终产品的食品。

lines.t: Ultra-processed foods are characteristically designed to be cheap, tasty, and convenient; examples include soft drinks and candy, packaged snacks and pastries, ready-to-heat products, and reconstituted meat products.
lines.cn: 超加工食品的典型特点是便宜、好吃、方便；例子包括软饮料和糖果、包装零食和糕点、即热食品，以及重组肉制品。

lines.t: Studies have linked consumption of ultra-processed foods—which are often high in salt, sugar, and fat—with weight gain and an increased risk of chronic diseases, even after adjusting for the amount of salt, sugar, and fat in the diet.
lines.cn: 研究已把超加工食品的摄入——它们通常高盐、高糖、高脂——与体重增加和慢性病风险上升联系起来，即便在调整了膳食中盐、糖、脂肪的摄入量之后依然如此。

lines.t: While the mechanisms behind these associations are not fully understood, Monteiro argues that the existing evidence is sufficient to justify discouraging consumption of ultra-processed foods in dietary recommendations and government policies.
lines.cn: 尽管这些关联背后的机制尚未完全弄清，蒙泰罗主张，现有证据足以支持在膳食建议和政府政策中不鼓励食用超加工食品。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 4 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do psychologists say people do when they are short of resources?

options.A: They begin to think of the benefits of constraints.
options.B: They try to seek solutions from creative people.
options.C: They try hard to maximize their mental energy.
options.D: They begin to see the world in a different way.

questions.cn: 心理学家说，当人们资源短缺时会怎样？

optionsCn.A: 他们开始想到限制的好处。
optionsCn.B: 他们试图从有创意的人那里寻求解决办法。
optionsCn.C: 他们努力最大化自己的心力。
optionsCn.D: 他们开始以不同的方式看待世界。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about innovation?

options.A: It is characteristic of all creative people.
options.B: It is essential to pushing society forward.
options.C: It is a creative person’s response to limitation.
options.D: It is an impetus to socio-economic development.

questions.cn: 关于创新，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它是所有创意人士的特点。
optionsCn.B: 它对推动社会前进至关重要。
optionsCn.C: 它是创意者对限制的回应。
optionsCn.D: 它是社会经济发展的动力。

questions.stem: What did a 2015 study by Ravi Mehta and Meng Zhu find?

options.A: Scarcity or abundance of resources has little impact on people’s creativity.
options.B: Innovative people are not constrained in connecting unrelated concepts.
options.C: People have no incentive to use available resources in new ways.
options.D: Creative people tend to consume more available resources.

questions.cn: 拉维·梅塔和朱蒙 2015 年的研究发现什么？

optionsCn.A: 资源的匮乏或充裕对人们的创造力影响甚微。
optionsCn.B: 有创新精神的人在连接不相关概念时不受约束。
optionsCn.C: 人们没有动力以新的方式使用现有资源。
optionsCn.D: 有创意的人倾向于消耗更多现有资源。

questions.stem: What did Marissa Mayer once write concerning creativity?

options.A: It is key to a company’s survival.
options.B: It shapes and focuses problems.
options.C: It is essential to meeting challenges.
options.D: It thrives best when constrained.

questions.cn: 关于创造力，玛丽莎·梅耶尔曾写下什么？

optionsCn.A: 它对公司生存至关重要。
optionsCn.B: 它塑造并聚焦问题。
optionsCn.C: 它对迎接挑战至关重要。
optionsCn.D: 它在受限制时最为旺盛。

lines.t: Believe it or not, human creativity benefits from constraints.
lines.cn: 信不信由你，人类的创造力得益于限制。

lines.t: According to psychologists, when you have less to work with, you actually begin to see the world differently.
lines.cn: 心理学家指出，当你能调用的东西更少时，你实际上会开始以不同的方式看待世界。

lines.t: With constraints, you dedicate your mental energy to acting more resourcefully.
lines.cn: 有了限制，你会把心力用于更善于利用现有资源地行动。

lines.t: When challenged, you figure out new ways to be better.
lines.cn: 面对挑战时，你会想出新的办法做得更好。

lines.t: The most successful creative people know that constraints give their minds the impetus to leap higher.
lines.cn: 最成功的创意人士都知道，限制给了他们的大脑跳得更高的动力。

lines.t: People who invent new products are not limited by what they don’t have or can’t do.
lines.cn: 创造新产品的人不会因自己缺少什么、做不到什么而受限。

lines.t: They leverage their limitations to push themselves even further.
lines.cn: 他们利用自身的局限把自己推得更远。

lines.t: Many products and services are created because the founders saw a limitation in what they use.
lines.cn: 许多产品和服务之所以被创造出来，是因为创始人看到了自己所使用的东西存在局限。

lines.t: They created innovation based on what was not working for them at the moment.
lines.cn: 他们基于当下对自己不好用的东西进行创新。

lines.t: Innovation is a creative person’s response to limitation.
lines.cn: 创新是创意者对限制的回应。

lines.t: In a 2015 study which examined how thinking about scarcity or abundance influences how creatively people use their resources, Ravi Mehta at the University of Illinois and Meng Zhu at Johns Hopkins University found that people simply have no incentive to use what’s available to them in novel ways.
lines.cn: 在 2015 年一项考察“思考匮乏或充裕如何影响人们创造性地使用资源”的研究中，伊利诺伊大学的拉维·梅塔和约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的朱蒙发现：人们根本没有动力以新颖的方式使用手头已有的资源。

lines.t: When people face scarcity, they give themselves the freedom to use resources in less conventional ways because they have to.
lines.cn: 当人们面对匮乏时，他们会给自己自由，用不那么常规的方式使用资源，因为他们不得不如此。

lines.t: Obstacles can broaden your perception and open up your thinking processes.
lines.cn: 障碍能拓宽你的感知，打开你的思维过程。

lines.t: Consistent constraints help you improve at connecting unrelated ideas and concepts.
lines.cn: 持续存在的限制有助于你提高把不相关的想法和概念联系起来的能力。

lines.t: Marissa Mayer, former vice president for search products and user experience at Google, once wrote in a publication on Bloomberg, “Constraints shape and focus problems and provide clear challenges to overcome; Creativity thrives best when constrained.”
lines.cn: 谷歌前搜索产品与用户体验副总裁玛丽莎·梅耶尔曾在彭博社的一篇文章中写道：“限制能塑造并聚焦问题，提供明确的挑战去克服；创造力在受限时最为旺盛。”

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 5 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker say strategies for managing conflicts can always be changed?

options.A: Because they are learned.
options.B: Because they come naturally.
options.C: Because they have to be properly personalized.
options.D: Because there can be more effective strategies.

questions.cn: 讲话者为什么说冲突处理策略总是可以改变的？

optionsCn.A: 因为它们是学来的。
optionsCn.B: 因为它们是天生的。
optionsCn.C: 因为它们必须被恰当个性化。
optionsCn.D: 因为可以有更有效的策略。

questions.stem: What is said to affect the way one acts in a conflict?

options.A: The extent of difference and of similarity between the two sides.
options.B: The knowledge of the specific expectation the other side holds.
options.C: The importance of one’s goals and of the relationship.
options.D: The approaches one adopts to conflict management.

questions.cn: 据说是什么影响着一个人在冲突中的行为方式？

optionsCn.A: 双方差异与相似的程度。
optionsCn.B: 对对方所持具体期待的了解。
optionsCn.C: 个人目标与这段关系的重要性。
optionsCn.D: 一个人采取的冲突管理方式。

questions.stem: Of the five styles the speaker discusses, which views conflicts as problems to be solved?

options.A: The fox.
options.B: The owl.
options.C: The shark.
options.D: The turtle.

questions.cn: 在讲话者讨论的五种风格中，哪一种把冲突看作有待解决的问题？

optionsCn.A: 狐狸型。
optionsCn.B: 猫头鹰型。
optionsCn.C: 鲨鱼型。
optionsCn.D: 乌龟型。

lines.t: Different people use different strategies for managing conflicts.
lines.cn: 不同的人用不同的策略应对冲突。

lines.t: These strategies are learned in childhood.
lines.cn: 这些策略是童年时期学会的。

lines.t: Usually, we are not aware of how we act in conflict situations.
lines.cn: 通常，我们并不清楚自己在冲突情境中是如何行事的。

lines.t: We just do whatever seems to come naturally.
lines.cn: 我们只是按看上去自然而然的方式去做。

lines.t: But we do have a personal strategy, and because it is learned, we can always change it by learning new and more effective ways of managing conflicts.
lines.cn: 但我们确实有一套个人策略，而正因为它是学来的，我们总可以通过学习新的、更有效的冲突处理方式来改变它。

lines.t: When you get involved in a conflict, there are two major concerns you have to take into account: achieving your personal goals and keeping a good relationship with the other person.
lines.cn: 当你卷入冲突时，有两个主要关切必须考虑：实现个人目标，以及与对方保持良好关系。

lines.t: How important your personal goals are and how important the relationship is to you affect how you act in a conflict.
lines.cn: 你的个人目标有多重要、这段关系对你有多重要，会影响你在冲突中的行为。

lines.t: Given these two concerns, five styles of managing conflicts can be identified.
lines.cn: 基于这两种关切，可以区分出五种冲突处理风格。

lines.t: The turtle.
lines.cn: 乌龟型。

lines.t: Turtles withdraw into their shells to avoid conflicts.
lines.cn: 乌龟会缩进壳里回避冲突。

lines.t: They give up their personal goals and relationships.
lines.cn: 他们放弃自己的个人目标和关系。

lines.t: They believe it is easier to withdraw from a conflict than to face it.
lines.cn: 他们认为逃避冲突比面对它更容易。

lines.t: The shark.
lines.cn: 鲨鱼型。

lines.t: Sharks try to overpower opponents by forcing them to accept their solution to the conflict.
lines.cn: 鲨鱼试图压制对手，迫使他们接受自己提出的冲突解决方案。

lines.t: They seek to achieve their goals at all costs.
lines.cn: 他们不惜一切代价达成自己的目标。

lines.t: Sharks assume that conflicts are settled by one person winning and one person losing.
lines.cn: 鲨鱼假定冲突的结局是一方赢、一方输。

lines.t: Winning gives sharks a sense of pride and achievement.
lines.cn: 获胜给鲨鱼带来自豪感和成就感。

lines.t: Losing gives them a sense of weakness, inadequacy, and failure.
lines.cn: 失败则给他们带来软弱、无能、失败的感觉。

lines.t: The teddy bear.
lines.cn: 泰迪熊型。

lines.t: Teddy bears want to be accepted and liked by other people.
lines.cn: 泰迪熊希望被他人接纳和喜欢。

lines.t: They think that conflict should be avoided in favor of harmony, and believe that conflicts cannot be discussed without damaging relationships.
lines.cn: 他们认为为了和谐应当避免冲突，并相信讨论冲突必然会损害关系。

lines.t: They give up their goals to preserve the relationship.
lines.cn: 他们放弃自己的目标以保全关系。

lines.t: The fox.
lines.cn: 狐狸型。

lines.t: Foxes are moderately concerned with their own goals and about their relationships with other people.
lines.cn: 狐狸对自己的目标和与他人的关系都适度关注。

lines.t: They give up part of their goals and persuade the other person in a conflict to give up part of his goals.
lines.cn: 他们放弃自己的部分目标，并说服冲突中的对方也放弃部分目标。

lines.t: They seek a solution to conflicts where both sides gain something.
lines.cn: 他们寻求让双方都有所收获的冲突解决方案。

lines.t: The owl.
lines.cn: 猫头鹰型。

lines.t: Owls view conflicts as problems to be solved.
lines.cn: 猫头鹰把冲突看作有待解决的问题。

lines.t: They see conflicts as improving relationships by reducing tension between two people.
lines.cn: 他们认为冲突能通过缓解两人之间的紧张关系来改善关系。

lines.t: They try to begin a discussion that identifies the conflict as a problem.
lines.cn: 他们努力开启一场把冲突认定为问题的讨论。

lines.t: By seeking solutions that satisfy both themselves and the other person, owls maintain the relationship.
lines.cn: 通过寻求既满足自己又满足对方的方案，猫头鹰维系了关系。

lines.t: Owls are not satisfied until a solution is found that achieves their own goals and the other person’s goals, and they are not satisfied until the tensions and negative feelings have been fully resolved.
lines.cn: 在找到既实现自己目标、又实现对方目标的方案之前，猫头鹰不会满意；在紧张和负面情绪被彻底化解之前，他们也不会满意。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 6 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do scientists hope to do by cracking the genetic code of plants and animals?

options.A: Help save species from extinction and boost human health.
options.B: Understand how plants and animals perished over the past.
options.C: Help gather information publicly available to researchers.
options.D: Find out the cause of extinction of Britain’s 66,000 species.

questions.cn: 科学家希望借助破译动植物基因编码做到什么？

optionsCn.A: 帮助物种免于灭绝并促进人类健康。
optionsCn.B: 了解动植物过去是如何消亡的。
optionsCn.C: 帮助收集向研究者公开的信息。
optionsCn.D: 查明英国 6.6 万物种灭绝的原因。

questions.stem: What do many scientists believe with regard to earth?

options.A: It was once dominated by dinosaurs.
options.B: It has entered the sixth mass extinction.
options.C: Its prospects depend on future human behaviour.
options.D: Its climate change is aggravated by humans.

questions.cn: 关于地球，许多科学家相信什么？

optionsCn.A: 它曾被恐龙主宰。
optionsCn.B: 它已进入第六次大灭绝。
optionsCn.C: 它的前景取决于人类未来的行为。
optionsCn.D: 它的气候变化被人类所加剧。

questions.stem: How does Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, describe the Darwin Tree of Life Project?

options.A: It dwarfs all other efforts to conserve, protect and restore biodiversity on earth.
options.B: It is costly to get started and requires the joint efforts of thousands of scientists.
options.C: It can help to bring back the large numbers of plants and animals that have gone extinct.
options.D: It is the most exciting, most relevant, most timely and most internationally inspirational.

questions.cn: 威康科学总监吉姆·史密斯爵士如何描述“达尔文生命之树计划”？

optionsCn.A: 它使所有其他保护、维护和恢复地球生物多样性的努力相形见绌。
optionsCn.B: 它启动成本高昂，需要数千名科学家的共同努力。
optionsCn.C: 它能帮助恢复大量已经灭绝的动植物。
optionsCn.D: 它是最令人兴奋、最切合实际、最及时、最能在国际上鼓舞人心的。

lines.t: The genetic code of all 1.5 million known species of animals and plants living on earth will be mapped to help save species from extinction and boost human health.
lines.cn: 地球上已知的 150 万种动植物，其基因编码都将被绘制出来，以帮助物种免于灭绝，并促进人类健康。

lines.t: Scientists hope that cracking the genetic code of plants and animals could help uncover new treatments for infectious diseases, slow aging, improve crops in agriculture, and create new bio-materials.
lines.cn: 科学家希望破译动植物的基因编码，能有助于发现传染病的新疗法、延缓衰老、改良农作物，并创造新的生物材料。

lines.t: In Britain, organisations including the Natural History Museum, the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew and the Wellcome Sanger Institute have joined forces to sequence Britain’s 66,000 species of animals and plants.
lines.cn: 在英国，自然历史博物馆、邱园皇家植物园和威康桑格研究所等机构已联合起来，对英国 6.6 万种动植物进行测序。

lines.t: Dubbed the Darwin Tree of Life Project, it is expected to take 10 years and cost £100 million.
lines.cn: 该项目被命名为“达尔文生命之树计划”，预计耗时 10 年、耗资 1 亿英镑。

lines.t: Once completed, all the information will be publicly available to researchers.
lines.cn: 一旦完成，所有信息都将向研究者公开。

lines.t: Many scientists believe that earth has now entered the sixth mass extinction, with humans creating a toxic mix of habitat loss, pollution and climate change, which has already led to the loss of at least 77 species of mammals and 140 types of birds since 1500.
lines.cn: 许多科学家认为，地球现已进入第六次大灭绝期：人类造成栖息地丧失、污染和气候变化的恶性组合，自 1500 年以来已导致至少 77 种哺乳动物和 140 种鸟类消失。

lines.t: It is the biggest loss of species since the dinosaurs were wiped out 66 million years ago.
lines.cn: 这是自 6600 万年前恐龙灭绝以来最大规模的物种丧失。

lines.t: Scientists say that sequencing every species will revolutionise the understanding of biology and evolution, bolster efforts to conserve as well as protect and restore biodiversity.
lines.cn: 科学家说，为每一个物种测序将彻底改变我们对生物学和进化的理解，推进保护、维护并恢复生物多样性的努力。

lines.t: Dr. Tim Littlewood, head of Life Sciences Department at the Natural History Museum, said, “Whether you are interested in food or disease, the history of how every organism on the planet has adapted to its environment is recorded in its genetic makeup.
lines.cn: 自然历史博物馆生命科学部主任蒂姆·利特尔伍德博士说：“无论你关心的是食物还是疾病，地球上每一种生物如何适应自身环境的历史，都记录在它的基因组成里。

lines.t: How you then harness that is dependent on your ability to understand it.
lines.cn: 而你能如何利用它，取决于你理解它的能力。

lines.t: We will be using modern methods to get a really good window on the present and the past.
lines.cn: 我们将用现代方法，真正打开一扇看清现在与过去的窗口。

lines.t: And of course, a window on the past gives you a prospective model on the future.”
lines.cn: 当然，一扇看清过去的窗口，也为你提供了一份关于未来的前瞻模型。”

lines.t: Sir Jim Smith, Director of Science at Wellcome, said, “Try as I might, I can’t think of a more exciting, more relevant, more timely or more internationally inspirational project.
lines.cn: 威康科学总监吉姆·史密斯爵士说：“我竭尽所能也想不出一个更令人兴奋、更切合实际、更及时、更能在国际上鼓舞人心的项目。

lines.t: Since 1970, humanity has wiped out 60 percent of animal populations.
lines.cn: 自 1970 年以来，人类已消灭了 60% 的动物种群。

lines.t: About 23,000 of 80,000 species surveyed are approaching extinction.
lines.cn: 在调查的 8 万个物种中，约有 2.3 万个正濒临灭绝。

lines.t: We are in the midst of the sixth great extinction event of life on our planet, which not only threatens wildlife species, but also imperils the global food supply.
lines.cn: 我们正处在地球生命第六次大灭绝事件之中，它不仅威胁野生物种，也危及全球粮食供给。

lines.t: As scientists, we all realise we desperately need to catalogue life on our fragile planet now.
lines.cn: 作为科学家，我们都意识到，我们迫切需要对这颗脆弱的行星上的生命进行编目。

lines.t: I think we’re making history.”
lines.cn: 我想我们正在创造历史。”

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 7 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is indeed just an illusion according to Professor Tom Oliver?

options.A: Cultural identity.
options.B: Social evolution.
options.C: The Copernican revolution.
options.D: Human individuality.

questions.cn: 根据汤姆·奥利弗教授，什么其实只是一种幻觉？

optionsCn.A: 文化身份。
optionsCn.B: 社会演化。
optionsCn.C: 哥白尼革命。
optionsCn.D: 人的个体性。

questions.stem: What does Professor Tom Oliver think of the idea that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe?

options.A: It is a delusion to be disposed of.
options.B: It is prevalent even among academics.
options.C: It is a myth spread by John Donne’s poem.
options.D: It is rooted in the mindset of the 17th century.

questions.cn: 汤姆·奥利弗教授如何看待“我们作为独立的自我存在于主观宇宙中心”这一想法？

optionsCn.A: 这是有待破除的错觉。
optionsCn.B: 它在学者中也普遍存在。
optionsCn.C: 这是约翰·多恩诗作传播的一个神话。
optionsCn.D: 它植根于 17 世纪的思维方式。

questions.stem: Why does Professor Tom Oliver claim that the material “us” is constantly changing?

options.A: He believes in Copernican philosophical doctrines about the universe.
options.B: He has gained ample scientific evidence at the University of Reading.
options.C: He has found that our inner self and material self are interconnected.
options.D: He contends most of our body cells can only live a few days or weeks.

questions.cn: 汤姆·奥利弗教授为什么声称物质意义上的“我们”始终在变化？

optionsCn.A: 他信奉关于宇宙的哥白尼哲学学说。
optionsCn.B: 他在雷丁大学获得了充分的科学证据。
optionsCn.C: 他发现我们的内在自我与物质自我是相互关联的。
optionsCn.D: 他主张我们身体的大多数细胞只能存活几天或几周。

questions.stem: How can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems according to Professor Tom Oliver?

options.A: By coming to see how disruptive such problems have got to be.
options.B: By realising that we all can do our own bit in such endeavours.
options.C: By becoming aware that we are part of a bigger world.
options.D: By making joint efforts resolutely and persistently.

questions.cn: 根据汤姆·奥利弗教授，我们怎样才能解决紧迫的环境和社会问题？

optionsCn.A: 通过认识到这些问题已经变得多么具有破坏性。
optionsCn.B: 通过认识到我们每人都能在此类努力中尽自己的一份力。
optionsCn.C: 通过意识到我们是一个更大世界的一部分。
optionsCn.D: 通过坚决而持久地共同努力。

lines.t: John Donne, the English poet, wrote in the 17th century, “No man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent, a part of the main.”
lines.cn: 英国诗人约翰·多恩在 17 世纪写道：“没有人是一座孤岛，能够自全；每个人都是大陆的一小块，是主体的一部分。”

lines.t: Now, a British academic has claimed that human individuality is indeed just an illusion, because societies are far more interconnected at a mental, physical, and cultural level than people realise.
lines.cn: 如今，一位英国学者宣称，人的个体性其实只是一种幻觉，因为各个社会在心理、物质和文化层面的相互联系，远比人们意识到的更紧密。

lines.t: In his new book, The Self Delusion, Professor Tom Oliver, a researcher in the Ecology and Evolution group at the University of Reading, argues there is no such thing as “self”, and not even our bodies are truly “us”.
lines.cn: 雷丁大学生态与进化研究组的汤姆·奥利弗教授在其新书《自我的错觉》中主张，并不存在所谓的“自我”，甚至连我们的身体也并非真正的“我们”。

lines.t: Just as Copernicus realised the Earth is not the centre of the universe, Professor Oliver said society urgently needs a Copernican-like revolution to understand people are not detached beings but rather part of one connected identity.
lines.cn: 奥利弗教授说，正如哥白尼认识到地球并非宇宙的中心，社会也迫切需要一场类似哥白尼式的革命，去理解人不是孤立的个体，而是一个相互连接的身份的一部分。

lines.t: “A significant milestone in the cultural evolution of human minds was the acceptance that the Earth is not the centre of the universe, the so-called Copernican Revolution,” he writes.
lines.cn: 他写道：“人类心智文化演化中的一个重要里程碑，是接受地球并非宇宙的中心，即所谓的哥白尼革命。”

lines.t: “However, we have one more big myth to dispose of: that we exist as independent selves at the centre of a subjective universe.
lines.cn: “然而，我们还有一个大的神话需要破除：我们作为独立的自我，存在于一个主观宇宙的中心。

lines.t: You may feel as if you are an independent individual, acting autonomously in the world; that you have unchanging inner self that persists throughout your lifetime, acting as a central anchor-point with the world changing around you.
lines.cn: 你也许觉得自己是一个独立的个体，在世界中自主行动；觉得自己有一个不变的、贯穿一生的内在自我，仿佛一个固定的锚点，而世界在它周围变化。

lines.t: This is the illusion I seek to tackle.
lines.cn: 这就是我试图破解的幻觉。

lines.t: We are intimately connected to the world around us.”
lines.cn: 我们与周围的世界紧密相连。”

lines.t: Professor Oliver argues there are around 37 trillion cells in the body but most have a lifespan of just a few days or weeks, so the material “us” is constantly changing.
lines.cn: 奥利弗教授指出，人体内约有 37 万亿个细胞，但大多数细胞的寿命只有几天或几周，所以物质意义上的“我们”始终在变化。

lines.t: In fact, there is no part of your body that has existed for more than 10 years.
lines.cn: 事实上，你身体里没有任何一个部分存在超过 10 年。

lines.t: “Since our bodies are essentially made anew every few weeks, the material in them alone is clearly insufficient to explain the persistent thread of an identity.”
lines.cn: “既然我们的身体基本上每隔几周就重造一次，那么仅凭其中的物质，显然不足以解释一条持续不断的身份线索。”

lines.t: Professor Oliver claims that individualism is actually bad for society, and only by realising we are part of a bigger entity can we solve pressing environmental and societal problems.
lines.cn: 奥利弗教授称，个人主义实际上对社会有害，只有认识到我们是一个更大整体的一部分，才能解决紧迫的环境和社会问题。

lines.t: Through selfish over consumption we are destroying the natural world and using non-renewable resources at an accelerating rate.
lines.cn: 通过自私的过度消费，我们正在毁掉自然界，并以越来越快的速度消耗不可再生资源。

lines.t: “We are at a critical crossroads as a species where we must rapidly reform our mindsets and behaviour to act in less selfish ways,” he said.
lines.cn: 他说：“作为物种，我们正处于关键的十字路口，必须迅速改变思维方式和行为，以不那么自私的方式行事。”

lines.t: “So let’s open our eyes to the hidden connections all around us.”
lines.cn: “所以，让我们睁开眼，看到周遭那些隐藏的联系吧。”
